title: One Line of Code Let the Kiosk See a Day, Not a Dot | vitalii.no
description:
A public kiosk display could only ever ask for the single latest glucose reading. Every other route on the hub, including the one holding history, returned a flat rejection — fine for showing one number on a TV, but it meant the screen could never show whether that number had been rising or falling through the day, only the most recent dot.

In the sugar hub's API (bridge/sugar_hub.py), I reordered the route checks so the history endpoint resolves before the kiosk's reject-everything gate, then added a clamp so any kiosk-scoped token gets its requested time window capped at 24 hours instead of being refused outright. Every other token keeps its existing 1-to-168-hour range untouched — only the public-facing kiosk scope was widened, and only up to a day.

One small reorder-and-clamp change took kiosk tokens from a single current reading to a full, bounded 24-hour history, with zero change to any other token's access.
